options.label: Reject Corvane and Award to Tasker & Moye
options.description: Reject Corvane Builders immediately based on statutory nonresponsiveness regarding missing licenses (C-16, C-20) and award the contract to Tasker & Moye as the lowest responsive bidder.

options.label: Reject All Bids and Re-bid
options.description: Reject all submitted bids to reset the procurement process, allowing the District to re-issue the Invitation to Bid with clarified specifications and updated licensing requirements.

options.label: Award to Tasker & Moye with Corvane as Subcontractor
options.description: Award the prime contract to Tasker & Moye while explicitly authorizing them to subcontract the General Building work to Corvane Builders, thereby maintaining compliance while utilizing local workforce capacity.

options.label: Reject Corvane and Award to Tasker & Moye
options.note: This course is unlawful because a bid cannot be rejected as nonresponsive solely for missing a subcontractor license if the prime bidder is a Class B general contractor who has the statutory right to subcontract the work, and it creates immediate exposure to a writ of mandate for denying Corvane a required hearing on the 'responsibility' issue regarding their prior termination.

options.label: Reject All Bids and Re-bid
options.note: While legally defensible as a last resort to cure ambiguous specifications, this option fails the client's needs by causing significant schedule delays and cost overruns, and it ignores the fact that the current bid pool likely contains a valid, responsive bidder (Tasker & Moye) who could proceed immediately.

options.label: Award to Tasker & Moye with Corvane as Subcontractor
options.note: This option is unlawful because it attempts to rewrite the bid evaluation after the fact by forcing a specific subcontractor relationship that was not part of the original bid evaluation, violating the fundamental principle of fair and equal treatment of bidders and creating a 'bid shopping' exposure.

grade.missing: An experienced practitioner would have immediately identified that the 'nonresponsiveness' claim regarding the C-16/C-20 licenses is likely meritless because a Class B general contractor is statutorily permitted to subcontract those trades, and would have recognized that the prior termination issue is a 'responsibility' determination requiring a formal hearing and notice under California law before any rejection can occur.
grade.overall: The colleague's advice failed to distinguish between facial nonresponsiveness and substantive responsibility determinations, leading to recommendations that either violate statutory bidding procedures or ignore the client's schedule constraints. A correct approach would have been to schedule a formal responsibility hearing for Corvane regarding their prior termination while simultaneously verifying that their bid is legally responsive as a Class B contractor with valid subcontractor plans.
